:::{#thm-pois-two-group-se}
#### Standard error of a two-group log rate ratio

Under the conditions of @thm-pois-two-group-mle,
the standard error of $\eb_1$ estimated from the inverse of the
[observed information matrix](https://morrison-lab.github.io/sds/intro-MLEs.html#def-oinf)
at $\evb$ is

$$
\ese{\eb_1} = \sqrt{\frac{1}{D_0} + \frac{1}{D_1}}
$$ {#eq-pois-two-group-se}

:::

::: proof
The observed information matrix is the negative Hessian of $\llik$,
so by @eq-pois-two-group-hessian,
evaluated at $\evb$:

$$
\underbrace{\oinff{\evb}}_{2 \times 2}
= \underbrace{\begin{bmatrix}
\emu_{\cdot 0} + \emu_{\cdot 1} & \emu_{\cdot 1} \\
\emu_{\cdot 1} & \emu_{\cdot 1}
\end{bmatrix}}_{2 \times 2}
$$

where $\emu_{\cdot k} \eqdef \sum_{i: x_i = k} t_i \el(k)$
is group $k$'s total fitted count.
By @thm-pois-two-group-mle,
each group's total fitted count equals its observed count:

$$
\ba
\emu_{\cdot k}
&= \el(k) \sum_{i: x_i = k} t_i
&& \text{(factor out the common rate)} \\
&= \frac{D_k}{T_k} \cdot T_k
&& \text{(fitted rate equals crude rate; definition of } T_k \text{)} \\
&= D_k
&& \text{(cancel } T_k \text{)}
\ea
$$

so

$$
\underbrace{\oinff{\evb}}_{2 \times 2}
= \underbrace{\begin{bmatrix}
D_0 + D_1 & D_1 \\
D_1 & D_1
\end{bmatrix}}_{2 \times 2}
$$

Its determinant is

$$
\ba
\det \oinff{\evb}
&= (D_0 + D_1) D_1 - D_1^2
&& \text{(} 2 \times 2 \text{ determinant formula)} \\
&= D_0 D_1 + D_1^2 - D_1^2
&& \text{(distribute)} \\
&= D_0 D_1
&& \text{(cancel)}
\ea
$$

and the $2 \times 2$ inverse formula
$\inv{\begin{bmatrix} a & b \\ c & d \end{bmatrix}}
= \frac{1}{ad - bc} \begin{bmatrix} d & -b \\ -c & a \end{bmatrix}$
gives

$$
\underbrace{\inv{\oinff{\evb}}}_{2 \times 2}
= \frac{1}{D_0 D_1}
\underbrace{\begin{bmatrix}
D_1 & -D_1 \\
-D_1 & D_0 + D_1
\end{bmatrix}}_{2 \times 2}
$$

The estimated variance of $\eb_1$ is the lower-right entry:

$$
\ba
\ese{\eb_1}^2
&= \frac{D_0 + D_1}{D_0 D_1}
&& \text{(lower-right entry of the inverse)} \\
&= \frac{D_0}{D_0 D_1} + \frac{D_1}{D_0 D_1}
&& \text{(split the numerator)} \\
&= \frac{1}{D_1} + \frac{1}{D_0}
&& \text{(cancel)}
\ea
$$

Taking the square root gives @eq-pois-two-group-se.
:::
